mcqs.q: In kittens undergoing OVH under ketamine-dexmedetomidine-midazolam, what did adding meloxicam plus intraperitoneal bupivacaine accomplish?
o: Increased the need for rescue analgesia
Almost eliminated the need for rescue analgesia
Had no effect on postoperative pain scores
mcqs.e: The multimodal group needed rescue analgesia in only 1/14 cats vs 15/15 controls.

mcqs.q: How did postoperative pain affect kittens in this trial?
o: It had no effect on eating
mcqs.e: The study concluded pain decreased food intake, with the multimodal group eating more.

mcqs.q: What does this trial suggest about opioid-free anesthesia for kitten OVH?
o: It can provide adequate pain relief when combined with multimodal analgesia
mcqs.e: The opioid-free protocol with multimodal analgesia produced adequate postoperative pain relief.

mcqs.q: The Spritztube evaluated in this study is what type of device, adapted for rabbits?
mcqs.e: The Spritztube is an extraglottic airway device originally developed for humans, here adapted as a supraglottic device for rabbits.

mcqs.q: How was correct Spritztube placement confirmed in all 14 rabbits?
mcqs.e: A capnographic wave and proximal cuff visualization confirmed placement in 14/14 rabbits; airflow detection only worked in 9/14.

mcqs.q: What was the principal complication reported with Spritztube placement?
mcqs.e: Only one of 14 rabbits developed respiratory distress after placement.

mcqs.q: What was the conclusion regarding undiluted intraperitoneal and incisional ropivacaine after major canine abdominal surgery?
o: It was not beneficial for postoperative analgesia
It eliminated the need for opioids
mcqs.e: Undiluted ropivacaine IP and incisional provided no analgesic benefit.

mcqs.q: Which group required rescue analgesia in this trial?
o: 3 of 8 dogs in the ropivacaine group and none in saline
mcqs.e: Rescue analgesia was given to 3/8 ropivacaine dogs and 0/8 saline dogs.

mcqs.q: Beyond sedation, what additional role of dexmedetomidine is highlighted in this review?
o: Effective analgesia, including as a locoregional adjuvant
mcqs.e: Dexmedetomidine is described as an effective analgesic and a locoregional anesthesia adjuvant that prolongs sensory block.

mcqs.q: What organ-protective properties does the review attribute to dexmedetomidine, supporting its use in critical care?
mcqs.e: The review cites potential neuroprotective, cardioprotective and vasculoprotective roles for trauma and septic patients.

mcqs.q: How does dexmedetomidine affect locoregional anesthesia when used as an adjuvant?
o: Increases the duration of the sensory block and reduces systemic analgesic demand
Has no effect on block duration
mcqs.e: As an adjuvant it increases sensory block duration and decreases demand for systemic analgesics.

mcqs.q: Adding a heated humidified breathing circuit to a warm water blanket had what effect on dogs undergoing OVH?
o: Reduced the incidence of postanesthetic hypothermia
Had no effect on body temperature
mcqs.e: The HHBC plus WWB combination reduced postanesthetic hypothermia.

mcqs.q: What was the incidence of hypothermia at extubation in the HHBC group versus controls?
mcqs.e: Hypothermia at extubation was 12.5% in the HHBC group vs 66.7% in controls.

mcqs.q: Comparing four endotracheal tube cleaning protocols, what did the study find?
o: No statistically significant differences between protocols
mcqs.e: Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences in post-cleaning bacterial growth between the four protocols.

mcqs.q: What did the survey reveal about ETT reuse practices among veterinary anesthesiologists?
o: Half of those reusing tubes did not sterilize them, with widely varying methods
mcqs.e: Half of respondents who reused ETTs did not sterilize them and cleaning methods varied widely with no evidence-based approach.

mcqs.q: What cardiovascular effect was observed with ketamine-dexmedetomidine plus local anesthesia for feline orchiectomy?
mcqs.e: Hypertension was observed intraoperatively across all groups.

mcqs.q: What effect did postoperative atipamezole have in this study?
o: Shortened anesthetic recovery with no difference between the two doses
Increased side effects at the higher dose
mcqs.e: Both atipamezole doses shortened recovery without differences between them or added side effects.

mcqs.q: When did the most rapid decline in body temperature occur in anesthetized dogs?
mcqs.e: The most rapid reduction in body temperature occurred within the first 15 minutes of anesthesia.

mcqs.q: What temperature pattern was seen from 60 to 240 minutes of anesthesia?
mcqs.e: After the initial decline, body temperature plateaued from 60 to 240 minutes.

mcqs.q: How did oral pregabalin compare to gabapentin for perioperative sedation in cats?
mcqs.e: At the doses studied the two drugs produced indistinguishable sedation and recovery effects.

mcqs.q: What did the trial find regarding emergence delirium and rescue sedation between the two drugs?
o: Both were infrequent and similar for both treatments
mcqs.e: Need for rescue sedation and emergence delirium were infrequent and similar for both treatments.

mcqs.q: What Bristol Rabbit Pain Scale score was determined as the practical cut-off for analgesic intervention?
mcqs.e: Analgesic intervention should be considered at a BRPS score of 5 or greater.

mcqs.q: How did the BRPS perform as a discriminator for the need for analgesia?
mcqs.e: The area under the ROC curve was 0.85, indicating excellent discrimination.

mcqs.q: Comparing meloxicam and robenacoxib after feline OVH, what did owner assessments suggest?
o: Both controlled pain, but meloxicam may have improved efficacy
mcqs.e: Both were effective, but the robenacoxib group had more abnormal behaviors and higher pain scores, suggesting meloxicam may be better in some cats.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about routinely sending all OVH cats home on NSAIDs?
o: A blanket prescribing approach may not be necessary
Owners cannot assess pain at all
mcqs.e: Most owners scored pain as 0, suggesting a blanket NSAID approach may not be needed, with cost and safety implications.

mcqs.q: What did this owner survey suggest about postoperative pain management after sterilization?
o: Cats may be undertreated for pain compared to dogs
Analgesics were prescribed for all pets
mcqs.e: The study concluded postoperative pain in cats may not be appropriately managed relative to dogs.

mcqs.q: What proportion of pets were prescribed analgesics at discharge in this high-volume clinic survey?
o: About 12% overall, with a numerically higher rate in dogs
mcqs.e: Analgesics were prescribed for 19/162 (12%) pets: 16% of dogs vs 6.7% of cats.
